corrections.raised_by: dispatcher stderr on the R1 VERIFY receipt (WARN_LANE_SERVED_UNASSIGNED_ARM), re-measured
corrections.earlier_claim: the three VERIFY rounds were nonce-attributed review turns on the mandated arm
corrections.measured: the arm they served (opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash) is NOT in the VERIFY_SECURITY assignment revision 44, which grants only ['gpt-6.1-sol','openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol']; the dispatcher warned SERVED_UNASSIGNED_ARM and a control run with --require-assigned-arms refused with ERR_NO_ASSIGNED_ARM (exit 4, before any model call)
corrections.why_it_happened: --force-rank resolves against the pool, so it outranks the assignment; the owner's 2026-11-14 task mandates deepseek for the checker while the assignment file (authority owner-order-20261022-r14) still grants gpt-6.1-sol, and the round used the pool to satisfy the mandate without recording the split
corrections.fix: every receipt now carries arm_in_assignment / assignment_arms / assignment_revision; the three verdicts are recorded as challenge records produced on an owner-mandated arm that the assignment does not grant — not as assignment-compliant operation and never as acceptance; the refusing control run is kept in out/LANE_VERIFY_ASSIGNED_ARMS_NEG.json；owner 裁定（OD-W1R2-1）：同模型非缺口、不得作為 PASS 阻斷，故本項保留為事實紀錄，不再列為缺口

No origin repository's `main` was written.
corrections.why_it_happened: the brief carried a hand-typed count, and the phrase 'no origin-repo write' conflated 'main untouched' with 'no write at all'
corrections.fix: report states the precise form: origin `main` untouched; one evidence branch + draft PR; one new private repo created on owner order. The counts in any future brief must be generated from the artefacts at dispatch time, not typed

corrections.earlier_claim: the write manifest's effects_not_performed listed 'origin repo write' and 'repo creation' as not performed
corrections.measured: an evidence branch + draft PR #60 exists on Fabric and shw097-team/FHS_vNEXT was created; the exclusions were false as written

corrections.earlier_claim: effect_boundary.performed_and_where listed repository creation with repo=null
corrections.measured: out/REPO_CREATE_READBACK.json carries the created repository as repo.full_name = shw097-team/FHS_vNEXT (and in steps[0].full_name, http 201); the derivation read a key that does not exist
corrections.why_it_happened: the readback schema nests the repo block; the code assumed a flat key, and a null slipped through
corrections.fix: derivation now reads repo.full_name, falls back to the 201 step, carries private/default_branch/head and the protection attempt; a null action/repo/receipt now raises instead of being written

corrections.earlier_claim: the manifest and the tree agree family-wide
corrections.measured: four manifest entries and the brief's size disagreed at review time, because the manifest hashed files that are regenerated during or after manifest generation (the brief, the review receipts, the manifest itself, the run's own stdout capture)
corrections.why_it_happened: no distinction between frozen artefacts and per-round volatile ones; a self-referential hash set cannot be consistent
corrections.fix: manifest now carries generated_at_utc and a declared volatile_excluded rule; every other file is hashed; build/manifest_check.py is read-only and recomputes all hashes (413 checked, 19 volatile excluded, drift 0 before dispatch)

corrections.earlier_claim: the manifest was generated last before dispatch
corrections.measured: it was not: docs/CORRECTIONS.json and build/gen_verify_brief.py were edited after it, so two hashes were stale at review time
corrections.why_it_happened: the corrections for a round were written after dispatching that round, which by definition mutates an already-frozen manifest
corrections.fix: the round order is now fixed and enforced: write every file (corrections, rulings, report inputs) → rebuild deliverables → generate manifest → manifest_check must return drift 0 → generate brief → dispatch. Nothing is edited after the manifest.
corrections.evidence: build/manifest_check.py output captured into out/MANIFEST_CHECK.txt before dispatch

corrections.earlier_claim: every manifest hash is recomputable by any reader
corrections.measured: the two relay credential files live in AppData and are not readable from a read-only review sandbox (PermissionError), so a reviewer's recomputation must report them as unreadable — which I had scored as drift
corrections.why_it_happened: the manifest did not distinguish 'hash I can verify' from 'declared file a reviewer cannot open'
corrections.fix: those entries now carry reader_visibility=RESTRICTED_CREDENTIAL_POOL plus a note; manifest_check lists them under unreadable_declared instead of drift, and the brief states that they are declared, not counted

corrections.earlier_claim: the volatile-exclusion rule covered everything written after the manifest
corrections.measured: it did not: the dispatch writes logs/*.txt, logs/attempts/*.txt and out/LANE_VERIFY_R*.attempts.ndjson after the manifest, so five files were neither declared nor excluded
corrections.why_it_happened: the rule was written for the brief only, not for the run-time tail that the dispatch itself produces
corrections.fix: volatile rule widened to lane_cwd/ (whole), logs/ (whole) and the lane receipts the dispatch writes; the manifest now also self-audits — files present but neither declared nor excluded must be 0 — and refuses to be considered complete otherwise

corrections.earlier_claim: nothing changes after the approval
corrections.measured: two hashed files changed after R10 approved: docs/CORRECTIONS.json (this append) and build/manifest_check.py (relative-path normalisation in the audit)
corrections.why_it_happened: the approval record itself must be written somewhere, and the audit needed a path fix to run at all
corrections.fix: both are declared by name in out/POST_APPROVAL_DELTA.json with their reasons; the delta record fails on any third, undeclared change; every one of the 352 approved files is re-hashed and must be identical
